title: Activity Selection
description: Learn how Greedy Algorithms maximize scheduling efficiency by selecting the best non-overlapping activities.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Scheduling problems appear frequently in computer science and real-world systems.

The Activity Selection Problem focuses on choosing the maximum number of non-overlapping activities from a larger collection.

Greedy Algorithms solve this efficiently by selecting activities strategically based on finishing times.

sections.title: Understanding the Activity Selection Problem
sections.content:
Each activity contains a start time and a finish time.

The goal is to select as many compatible activities as possible without overlapping schedules.

Once an activity is selected, overlapping activities can no longer be chosen.

sections.title: The Greedy Scheduling Strategy
sections.content:
The greedy approach sorts activities according to their finishing times.

The algorithm first selects the activity that finishes earliest.

Afterward, it repeatedly selects the next activity that starts after the previously selected activity ends.

This strategy maximizes the remaining available time for future activities.

sections.title: Why Earliest Finish Time Works
sections.content:
Choosing activities that finish earlier leaves more room for additional activities later.

This greedy decision increases the probability of selecting the maximum number of compatible activities.

The strategy succeeds because local optimization aligns correctly with the global objective in this problem.

sections.title: Meeting Schedule Analogy
sections.content:
Imagine scheduling meetings inside a conference room.

If shorter meetings are selected first, more meetings can fit throughout the day.

Selecting long meetings too early may block many future opportunities.

This reflects the logic behind activity selection.

sections.title: Scheduling Systems in Real Applications
sections.content:
Scheduling optimization is important in operating systems, event management, airline scheduling, manufacturing systems, and network resource allocation.

Greedy scheduling algorithms help maximize efficiency while minimizing conflicts and wasted resources.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
sections.content: The Activity Selection Problem uses a greedy scheduling strategy to maximize the number of compatible activities. By selecting activities with the earliest finishing times, the algorithm efficiently optimizes scheduling opportunities.
